articles.title: What NFL stars’ zodiac signs say about their 2026 seasons: Pisces Justin Herbert, Cancer AJ Brown, and Leo Jalen Hurts
articles.summary: An Instagram account called “Sportsish” shared a post on “Which NFL player do you share your zodiac sign with?” It had Justin Herbert, AJ Brown, and Jalen
articles.body: An Instagram account called “Sportsish” shared a post on “Which NFL player do you share your zodiac sign with?” It had Justin Herbert, AJ Brown, and Jalen Hurts, among others. The most interesting part was how each player’s gridiron traits matched typical zodiac-sign traits.Could the signs explain why NFL stars look calm under pressure - while others seem fueled by emotion, confidence, or perfectionism? Probably not. But astrology does add a fun twist to the 2026 NFL season.Three prominent names - Justin Herbert, AJ Brown, and Jalen Hurts - have three different zodiac personalities. Their performances will be judged by football, preparation, and circumstances. But their zodiac signs provide an intriguing way to look at the start of their 2026 season.Justin Herbert’s four loss start could fuel Pisces’ resilience traitJustin Herbert was born on March 10. He’s a Pisces, a water sign known for being intuitive, adaptable, humble, and resilient. The 2026 season has shown a different side of him.He entered Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks with a 0-3 record. He lost that game 30-23, leaving the Los Angeles Chargers at 0-4. For any typical Pisces, adversity is an opportunity to regroup. Herbert’s zodiac sign makes him want to channel his frustration into patience and creativity, thereby giving rise to a quiet bounce-back.As for Sportsish’s notes, Herbert broke an NFL rookie record with 31 touchdowns - that speaks to “intuitive.” He was thrown into the Hollywood sparkle surrounding his relationship with Madison Beer. This equals “adaptable.”As for the “humble” trait, Herbert broke the rookie touchdown record but said that winning mattered more than the record.AJ Brown’s interrupted season could compare to Cancer’s emotional depthAJ Brown was born on June 30. He’s a Cancer, another water sign known for being protective, intuitive, loyal, and emotionally connected. His 2026 chapter began with a blockbuster trade from the Philadelphia Eagles to the New England Patriots.But in his first game of the season, he got off to a frustrating start. He caught only three passes for 26 yards before an ankle injury cut his season short and sent him to injured reserve.For a zodiac sign known for emotional depth, resilience, and retreating into its shell after setbacks, the sudden interruption could have been difficult. But if he could just hold onto himself and stay loyal to his game, he could come back in a never-seen-before form.According to Sportsish, AJ Brown won a Super Bowl after four straight 1,000-yard seasons in Philadelphia - this speaks to a “passionate” trait. He played through injuries and could still record impeccable stats. This equals the “resilient” trait.He reunited with head coach Mike Vrabel after playing for him with the Tennessee Titans. This gives a shoutout to the “loyal” trait.Jalen Hurts could channel Leo’s confidence to avoid three peat lossJalen Hurts was born on August 7. This makes him a Leo, a fire sign associated with confidence, leadership, ambition, and a burning desire to perform on the biggest stage. This perfectly defines an NFL quarterback.Hurts’ 2026 season began with two wins but fell to two crucial losses as the season went on. The Philadelphia Eagles lost to the Chicago Bears in Week 3 and then to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4.Hurts threw 3 touchdowns against Los Angeles, but eventually fell short of four points [24-20]. Classic Leo: confidence after setbacks. This is his chance to make an astounding comeback in Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.As per Sportsish, Jalen Hurts won Super Bowl MVP and brought another championship to Philadelphia - this is his “confident” trait from the Leo zodiac sign catalog. He went from being benched at Alabama to becoming an NFL superstar. This screams “determined” trait.He surrounded himself with a bada*s, all-female team that negotiates record-breaking deals. This equals an “ambitious” trait. He became one of the faces of the NFL but still stayed himself. articles.title: After Impressing Celtics Teammates, Baylor Scheierman Eyes Bigger Role
articles.summary: Baylor Scheierman is ready to show what he can really do with the Celtics if given the opportunity.
articles.body:
Baylor Scheierman earned more opportunities in his second season with the Celtics last year. He found confidence and took advantage when those opportunities arose. Now, he aims to build on that.

Entering year three, Scheierman is in a unique situation. The Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George. Boston also signed Mike Conley. Jayson Tatum is the leader, while Payton Pritchard looks to have another breakout season.

The shooter, who played for South Dakota State and Creighton, has been training hard heading into the 2026-27 season, and star players and veterans, like Conley and Pritchard, have taken notice.

"The other day, Baylor, I think I got like four offensive rebounds in one possession, and I just said, 'I like him,'" Conley told SI . "Like that's all I need to know. I like him. I like him a lot. And obviously, he did a bunch of other things other than that. But his willingness to crash and keep possessions alive and make the right reads was impressive. Stuff like that sticks out to me."

"He's been really good," Pritchard said. "Like just really good in the areas, like the margins. His game's grown. Obviously, he's always been a good shooter, good floater, stuff like that. But he will be really important for this team this year."

The former Summit League Player of the Year and All-Big East honoree was selected with the 30th pick by the Celtics in the 2024 NBA Draft. In 31 games during the 2024-25 season, Scheierman averaged 3.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 0.5 steals per game. In 77 games last season, he averaged 5.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 0.5 steals per game.

Given the chance to prove himself, Scheierman increased his value. He's ready to do that in preseason play. Scheierman appreciates those who give him his flowers. The 26-year-old is ready to show what he can really do if given the opportunity.

"It's really about attacking every single day, and with whatever opportunity you get, kind of making the most of it," Scheierman said. "You start the year not really knowing what's going to happen, and you get a little opportunity here, you try to make the most of it, and with that, more opportunity comes.

"And so, whatever opportunity I'm given, I have the most confidence in myself that I'll be able to impact the game in whatever way."
